reviews.text: 类亿万僵尸 玩了demo感觉良好 大意了没有战役模式 先试试远征 另外每次开局时 遇到神殿都是打不过的要绕开 而基地固定在地图中间 开局时四通八达 各个方向都有打不过的神殿 设计不是很认同 更新评测 兵种只有4种 但有大量局外成长 全靠局外成长加持兵种特性 远征模式随机奖励玩家阵营 随机增强敌人阵营 但是太短只能打3场遭遇战 没有战役模式 非常需要战役模式!!!!!!!!!!!!! 道路是开发商设计的核心 用于加速移动 连接建筑 防止建筑堵死无法通过 我估计开发商不会改掉 投射物不会被城墙等障碍物阻挡 守城比"要战便战"爽很多 高难度开局艰难 要配合城墙攻克靠近基地的初始敌人聚落 但度过开局后纯爽 兵力成型比亿万僵尸要快的多 rts手感不错 可以甩枪兵 甚至还有兴奋剂科技 优化不错 不会卡

tldr: If you like killing lots of bugs and are looking for a solid game to do so, this is it. [hr][/hr] I've been fortunate enough to be part of this game from an early stage as a playtester and have already spent many hours on it and I love it. It's great at so many things. Want to kill thousands of things? Just start up a skirmish game. Think it's too hard? Just set the difficulty down and try again. Not hard enough? Crank it all the way up to infestation 5. Want some randomization? Play an expedition for incremental changes per map. Want to see how far you can get against infinitely scaling enemies? Give Endless mode a try. And don't worry if you don't think you have the micro to manage it all. Just pause the game and give out all your orders in your own time. I for sure need it :P The game also supports a bunch of playstyles with their deity system. Want to be turtling your way to victory? Go Tiamman which enhances your towers and walls. Want to have a mass of units and just clear the whole map? Play Karkadann which boosts your unit production and strength. Then there is the costumisation. As you play the game you unlock more and more powerups which you can get access to throughout your games. They can completely change your playstyle, from adding reflect damage to your knights to making your healers into killing machines. Your ballista towers can turn in to basically a shotgun shooting 5 bolts at a time. To me this has been a great way to spend my time, from being able to just chill in an easy skirmish to go full sweat in infestation 5 endless no-pauze mode. In terms of it being early access this game feels very well put together. Generally there are maybe some minor bugs which the devs are actively working on fixing. They've also been active on the discord, taking part in conversations. That much is apparent with each patch they bring out which always improves the game in one way or another often taking into account suggestions and feedback which were given on the Discord. The game itself runs smoothly, the units just do what you tell them to do (well, almost always). The large swarms of enemies feel fun to play against. Your upgrades feel very impactful and you can make so many different builds which can cater to any playstyle you'd like. For the price, you won't regret this. Even if the game stays in the state it currently is. But better yet, they're still going to add more content. Which is going to make this game even more fun.

一、亮眼优点：感官与玩法双在线，虫群对抗氛围感拉满 首先必须夸一夸游戏的画面、音效与怪物设计，这三大块是这款游戏最圈粉的地方。画面风格简洁又不失张力，虫族怪物的建模细节很到位，不同种类的虫子特征鲜明，无论是普通爬虫、飞行虫还是后期的遁地虫，外形辨识度极高，虫群密集来袭时的视觉压迫感很强，配合流畅的战斗特效，攻防对战的视觉效果很过瘾。 音效方面更是加分项，虫子爬行的沙沙声、攻击时的嘶吼声、炮塔开火的轰鸣、城墙破损的碎裂声，搭配贴合紧张氛围的背景音乐，完美营造出末日抵御虫潮的沉浸感，每一波攻势来袭时，音效都能把紧张感拉满，代入感特别强。而且游戏里的怪物机制设计很有层次感，不同虫子有不同的攻击方式和弱点，倒逼玩家合理布局防线、搭配兵种，策略性完全不弱。 再说说游戏节奏，我主打困难无尽模式，整体节奏偏快，但节奏把控很合理，完全不像《亿万僵尸》那样一旦失误就直接崩盘“开饭”。大部分时候即便防线出现缺口，都有足够的操作空间和挽救机会，能通过调整兵种站位、紧急修补城墙、集火关键怪物来逆转局势，这种“险中求胜”的体验，比一味的快节奏碾压更有乐趣，也让无尽模式的耐玩度大幅提升。 另外值得一提的是，我全程游玩下来没有遇到任何BUG，游戏稳定性很不错，没有出现卡顿、闪退或者机制异常的情况，对于独立游戏来说，这份完成度已经非常难得。 二、现存不足：细节瑕疵影响实战体验，亟待优化完善 虽然整体好评，但游玩过程中也发现了几个影响操作手感和游戏体验的问题，最突出的就是兵种AI寻路逻辑不完善。很多时候我方兵种明明有更便捷、更安全的近路可以走，偏偏会绕远路冲进密集的虫群堆里，平白无故承受伤害，甚至直接暴毙，尤其是在无尽模式后期，兵力本身紧张，这种无效减员很影响防线稳固，也打乱了原本的布局策略，希望制作组能重点优化寻路算法，让兵种走位更智能、更贴合实战需求。 其次是遁地虫机制过于强势，破坏防线后难以补救。困难无尽模式后期遁地虫登场后，这个问题尤为明显：一旦城墙被它破坏，只要没能第一时间彻底消灭这只遁地虫，损坏的围墙就完全无法修补，它会持续不断地召唤小规模虫群，源源不断地冲击缺口，慢慢蚕食整个防线。这种机制有点过于强硬，缺少缓冲空间，往往一次没处理好遁地虫，之前苦心搭建的防线就会逐步崩溃，建议适当调整遁地虫的召唤频率或围墙修复机制，平衡难度。 还有一点小遗憾，前期可使用的兵种种类偏少，前期玩法和阵容搭配相对单一，只能靠基础兵种和基础防御设施过渡，一定程度上影响了前期的玩法丰富度，期待后续能新增前期兵种，让前期发育阶段也有更多策略选择。 三、总结与期待：潜力无限，会持续关注支持 总而言之，《虫群来袭》是一款优点远大于缺点的优质独立游戏，核心玩法成熟、感官体验出色，难度设计适中，耐玩度和策略性都在线，有着成为爆款塔防生存游戏的潜力。我个人会继续深耕困难无尽模式，也真心推荐喜欢塔防、生存、虫潮对抗题材的玩家入手尝试，希望这款游戏能被更多人看到、被更多玩家喜爱。 最后也期待制作组能够持续更新优化，重点完善AI寻路、平衡遁地虫机制、扩充兵种阵容，不断打磨细节，让这款游戏变得更加完美！ --- English Gameplay Experience Here Comes The Swarm: A Promising Tower Defense Survival Gem with Room for Improvement I’ve recently dived into Here Comes The Swarm, a tower defense and survival game, and my overall experience has been surprisingly positive. As a niche indie title, it boasts huge potential, with solid core gameplay and immersive sensory design. Even with a few flaws holding it back, I’m still eager to keep playing and exploring. Below is my honest review based on hours of gameplay in Hard Endless Mode, covering its strengths, weaknesses and my expectations for the future. I. Standout Strengths: Immersive, Strategic and Highly Polished First and foremost, the game’s visuals, sound design and enemy creature creation are easily its biggest highlights. The art style is crisp and dynamic, with highly detailed, distinct models for every type of bug—from basic crawlers and flying pests to the late-game burrowing bugs. Each creature has a unique design, and when swarms close in, the visual pressure is intense; paired with smooth combat effects, the offensive and defensive battles feel thrilling and satisfying. The sound design elevates the experience even further. The rustle of crawling bugs, their screeching attacks, the roar of turret fire, and the crack of broken walls all blend perfectly with a tense, atmospheric soundtrack, fully drawing players into the post-apocalyptic bug-fighting setting. Every wave of enemies ramps up the tension through audio alone, creating incredible immersion. What’s more, the enemy mechanics are layered and well-thought-out: different bugs have unique attack patterns and weaknesses, forcing players to plan defenses carefully and combine units strategically, adding solid depth to the gameplay. In terms of pacing, Hard Endless Mode feels fast but well-balanced. Unlike They Are Billions, where one small mistake leads to an instant, unavoidable defeat, this game gives players plenty of chances to recover. Even if your defenses are breached, you can adjust unit positions, quickly repair walls, and focus fire on key threats to turn the tide. This “clutch recovery” feel makes endless mode far more replayable and enjoyable than pure, unforgiving speed. Another big plus: Iencountered zero bugs or glitches during my entire playtime. The game runs smoothly with no crashes, freezes or mechanical errors—an impressive level of stability for an indie release. II. Key Flaws: Minor Shortcuts That Hurt Gameplay Flow For all its strengths, I noticed a few critical issues that harm the gameplay experience, most notablypoor unit AI pathfinding. Far too often, my units will ignore clear, safe, short paths and instead charge straight into dense swarms of bugs, taking unnecessary damage or even dying instantly. In late-game Endless Mode where every unit counts, this needless loss cripples defenses and ruins careful strategies. I strongly hope the developers refine the pathfinding AI to make unit movement smarter and more battle-ready. Second, the burrowing bug mechanic is overly punishing and leaves no room for recovery. Once burrowing bugs appear in late Hard Endless, a single breach in your walls becomes a permanent problem: if you fail to eliminate the burrower immediately, you cannot repair the damaged wall at all. The burrowing bug will continuously spawn small waves of bugs, pouring through the gap and slowly tearing your entire defense apart. This mechanic feels far too unforgiving, with no buffer for error; one misstep can undo all your hard work. I suggest adjusting the burrower’s spawn rate or adding a way to repair walls under pressure to balance the difficulty. Lastly, early-game unit variety is too limited. The early stages only offer basic units and defenses, leading to repetitive strategy and less engaging progression. Adding more early-game unit options would make the opening phase more dynamic and give players more tactical choices right from the start. III. Final Thoughts & Expectations All in all, Here Comes The Swarm is a fantastic indie game with far more strengths than flaws. It has polished core gameplay, great immersion, balanced difficulty, and massive potential to become a standout in the tower defense survival genre. I will keep playing and mastering Hard Endless Mode, and I fully recommend it to anyone who loves tower defense, survival, or bug-swarm combat. I truly hope more players discover and support this game. I also look forward to future updates from the development team: refining AI pathfinding, balancing the burrowing bug mechanic, expanding the unit roster, and polishing small details to make this already great game even better!

EA review, 2026 March Very similar to "There are billions", except teching up is more troublesome, there's no campaign, storyline or characters of any sort, upgrades are also more troublesome, every mission has a time limit (auto win if you survive that long) which generally means there's no time to tech up or explore more than just a portion of each map. Expeditions (chains of missions) are randomized. Mission maps are randomized. Does that increase replayability? No, because you're still doing the same thing over and over again, in pretty much the exact same sequence, regardless of map differences. Instead, you get a lot of badly designed maps. If you survive a certain amount of time, you win! Yay... but that actually means you got no time to get anything done. No time to explore and grab those rewards and meta upgrades. No time to tech up. Pause function is only marginally useful since the real limiter is resource generation. Ultimately this means repeating tech 1 skirmishes, the same construction sequences over and over again, grinding toward unlocking upgrades that you don't have the time to deploy in each mission. Lack of campaign, storyline, and characters hurt. Lack of good mission design and map design hurt. This grind feels like I'm going nowhere and even the stuff I unlock feels useless. I miss "They Are Billions". Heck, I'm going back to it now...

Game's logic is like They Are Billions. I think it is more smooth and fun to play compared to Age of Darkness but still have issues. Lack of campaign feels bad. Closest thing to it is called Expeditions which is several missions with buffs and negatives you can choose to impact rest of the missions but I think they are terribly balanced and the RNG plays a big factor on gameplay due to map's shape. Arcanum upgrades feels like the meta progression, has a nice logic but it needs work to be more useful in the game. In They Are Billions, you could unlock many buildings, starting bonuses and new technologies as you progressed through the campaign. In Here Comes the Swarm, you already have everything unlocked so instead you can get buffs between missions but they feel weak. Because enemies also get buffs and you recieve some penalties. So while your units' all stats stays the same, enemies get boost to all their stats. Units' power drops significantly even with all the upgrades as you progress in the late game. Most of the time you have to use hit-and-run tactics to avoid losing units. That consumes time and leaves you little time to explore before the next wave hits. Towers also feel weak on late game. Tİme between waves needs to broader give room to do other stuff. Tunneler enemy needs work. As they spawn enemies too fast and powerful in the late game to counter. Several Tunnelers at once is a even worse nightmare. Units' pathing also needs work. Sometimes they stuck or follow ridicilous routes within city or narrow passages. It would be better if roads were more obivous, visible. Because of the terrain or buildings, sometimes they blend in. Overall, I must admit I am a bit disappointed with the game but still hopeful it will come around as it is still early access. Right now although it was a nice change, I can't really recommend this game.

Updating my Review after losing a whole day to this game. First of all not at all an RTS guy but this subgenre itches something in my head. This game is everything that "They are Billions" should've been, progression is good and does not feel like a chore, the rougelite gameplay loop is super fun, trying out new tactics with the 2 deities (a third one is on its way). The Essences can upgrade your Units/Towers drastically so placing them strategically in your Deity screen is key. but there are three things that really bother me 1. please add an option to disable or lessen the amount of unit chatter after playing a unit based build for 3 skirmishes it really gets annyoing 2. the pathfinding from both the enemies and the player units is sometimes horrendous. 3. Biome variety, you can select your map type but I think its just what ressource is the dominant one (stone, wood and a mix of both), the map always looks the same, same trees, same ground texture and so on Please dont try to add a Campaign. It doesn't work for this kind of game.

三次编辑了，很好的游戏，期待更新！期待更多人发现宝藏！ (————————————————） 打到侵袭3的远征了，但是开了七八把了，没一把能通关。 感觉目前对我来说的难点有两个，第一个是资源：前期的发育至关重要，主要是缺木头，目前感觉这一块太吃运气了：要么地图很好，木头很多，木材厂位置好，或者有小花园；要么宝箱里面出木头很多。但是这俩玩意儿都很吃运气。有一把侵袭3最后一关的惩罚是降低视野，好不容易出去一看根本没木头，直接断发育。死的挺憋屈的。 第二个难点就是入侵的强度：一般来说我蛮犀图腾最后守家也不得不用投石机和石墙，但是敌方的强度过高，点名那个大毒蝎，对防线的冲击力有点太强了。打到侵袭3的倒数第二关的时候就已经非常吃力了。 这个游戏作为防守游戏，要做好再能守住的前提下尽可能地贪发育。但是现在初期守家资源和中期发育资源都很看运气，感觉需要一些调整。 （————————————————） 第一次编辑：打过了侵袭3的远征，心得体会就是，远征中点出前期强力天赋真的很关键，特别是金色树木、核心的金钱和气体收入这些，能够很大程度解放前期的经济需求，让地图的随机性影响降低。准备开始攻略侵袭4了。 毒蝎虽然强，但是还好每波入侵也就1只，可以利用暂停让防御塔集火，争取让毒蝎只喷出1~2次，对防线的威胁就不算很大 还有就是侵袭3的敌人强度已经相当高了，3分钟一波的入侵很难在nosl的情况下稳定守住，很多时候需要通过不停地sl，先看到每一波入侵的来向，再sl提前调集防御力量。这确实多少算是在作弊了，但想不到要怎样稳定守住每一波。3分钟一波，每波只给30秒的反应时间，临时调兵挺难的。只能说每次得提前预备好，然后打完一边就布防一边，经济好稳扎稳打，还是能打的。 （——————————————） 第二次编辑 终于拿下，侵袭5难度的远征，用的这一套： D1E27E36E43E41E33E31E10E40E32E54E51E77N骑士转投石机 前期：蛮犀图腾确实厉害，前期推图能力一流，发育滚雪球越早，对我们越有利。先把家门口的木头气体采一采，然后兵营造出来造几个骑士，大概造4个骑士配合初始兵，就可以把初级的圣坛和虫巢都磨下来。操作也很简单，把带着指挥官圣物的骑士往前顶，受到多个虫子攻击的骑士往后拉，每个骑士基本上都可以抗住1个成虫的攻击，这就够了。 5分钟的时候，地图边缘会开始不停地出兵骚扰我们，前期每一个路口只需要一个骑士巡逻就可以守住，大概7~8个骑士+7~8个弩手，找一个狭窄一点的路口（或者配合木墙），就可以守住7分半的第一波进攻和10分钟的第二波进攻。兵力持续生产到推图的兵力有15个左右骑士和12个左右弩手，通过合理的操作基本就可以推掉绝大多数营地了，但是侵袭5的孵化者守着的圣坛最好别碰，要打很久，而且很容易和周围的虫巢产生联动。 经济方面，大概要有15左右的气体收入，以及40左右的木头收入，科技先点伐木场和精炼厂增效，然后直接升石器时代。 中期：中期的关键就是要找到合适的房区，一片平坦、开阔的区域用来放大量的房子、屠宰场和教堂、酒馆，这是整个流程收入的重要保障。这个区域最重要的一点是，外围最好只有数个小路口，方便中期发育的同时进行防守。20分钟之后，骚扰的兵力会逐步明显增强，这个时候要用箭塔和墙体来协助防守各个小路口。 石器时代之后的第一要务是要造出市场，然后为了推图可以适量造出3~5个牧师，以及10个左右的纵火狂。中期的防御靠木墙、箭塔和纵火狂也基本上都能守住。 后期：等到图腾精华全部点完，就来到了后期。这个时候后期的第一生产建筑，注能器就可以开始使用了。 注能器的强度非常恐怖，配合注能加时75%的精华，基本上可以让整个游戏的后期都处于注能的状态中。 注能最好用的就是血红宝石，因为平时显示的经济收入是（收入-支出），而注能之后，经济收入会变成（2*收入-支出）这是非常夸张的。我打侵袭5的时候，通常收入显示+1000，实际上是2000的收入减去1000的维护费。而注能之后，则变成4000的收入减去1000的维护费，我们的经济收入直接变成+3000。而多出来的钱直接在市场购买资源。侵袭5远征的最后一关，+3000的经济就已经足够建立防线了。 至于防线，首推投石机，没有之一。很难想象要怎么用纵火狂防守侵袭5，但是投石机加上箭塔可以轻松做到。投石机输出高，手长，真群攻。每一处防线有3~4个投石机的火力，再加上一排箭塔和不断补充的3~5排木墙，基本都是够用的。箭塔优先攻击最高血量的蛮兽，每一波虫潮都操作防御塔优先点掉毒蝎，则防线无忧矣。 （——————————————） 图腾：D1E27E36E43E41E33E31E10E40E32E54E51E77N骑士转投石机 思路：初始点用吸血骑士，配合蛮犀的指挥官天赋和对兵的强化，可以轻松配合弩手推图。可以说是性价比最高的精华（essence）点了。 然后按顺序点如下精华： 1.降低激活精华需求2点。右边绿色天赋（talent）点出防御塔射程。——防御塔是后期的防御主力，在高难度下，我认为投石机是最有效的后期防御手段。而射程有助于箭塔和投石机协助推图，以及在每波虫潮来袭时手动集火毒蝎。 2.提升圣坛精华2点。右边蓝色天赋点出20食物，红色天赋两边都行。——这两个天赋是为了快速提升精华等级，并且获取尽可能高的总精华数，维持后期注能器的持续运行。食物是前期发育最容易卡的资源。 3.单位降价30%。——这个比红色天赋厉害不少，因为是所有资源降低30%，对于骑士来说，3木头和气体变成2木头和气体，等效降价33%。而气体相对来说是前期很匮乏的资源。 4~10.剩下的可以根据实际需求点：无敌盾和骑士被动技能有助于推图；增强墙体血量和降低墙体造价有助于配合墙体构筑防线；注能相关的强化都是为了维持注能器的运转。 右边红色天赋选择单位射程，用于中期纵火狂推图；蓝色天赋点教堂酒馆范围以便布局，并且可以节省地皮，科技降价对解锁建筑和兵种的研究是无效的，不知道是不是bug。12级蓝色天赋一定选血红宝石+50%产量，配合注能器再+100%，有钱了什么资源都可以去市场买。7级绿色天赋点墙体血量100，因为我们精华已经有墙体降价了，木墙只需要1木头就可以建造。木墙是完全可以从头用到尾的，把石头用于更珍贵的建筑升级以及投石机的建造中吧。 11.远戍（farwatch）。这个精华的强化幅度很高，推图的时候如果主推一边，一般来说能让聚落规模达到70+，也就是等效35%的防御塔攻击力。这个精华也是要后期发力，所以我们后期再点。建筑攻击力的精华非常重要。 12.投石机射程+14和弹道速度+75%。夸张的精华，也是投石机强大的重要来源。满射程的投石机可以覆盖多条防线，每个防线2~3个投石机，可以在多个防线相互支援，这是非常有效的防御手段。投石机最好设置最近目标，虫潮来袭的时候瞄准最前的目标，如果目标没有被木墙挡住，那么投石机自然也会砸到后面的虫潮，不至于浪费输出。 绿色天赋一定点建筑攻速+30%，毋庸置疑。于是乎，我们在后期就拥有了+30%攻速，+16射程，+30~40%攻击力的投石机，每一台仅仅需要300钱、50木头、15气体和10石头，从头用到尾，你值得拥有！ （————————————————） 非常好的游戏，期待更新，也期待更多人发现它的魅力！

While I understand that the game is still in early access and active development, right now playing it induces more annoyment than fun. I've played many similar games ([b]From Glory to Goo, TAB, Diplomacy is not an Option[/b], etc.) with similar gameplay loop (explore-expand-defend) so I have something to compare [b]HCTS[/b] with. [h3]The things that I like:[/h3] [olist] [*]Nice and clear graphics, units, buildings, terrain and POI's are quite distinguishable. [*]Unit control is responsive on Starcraft-like level, however lacks some features (more on that later) [*]It is very nice to have expeditions mode, would like to see more improvements and meta-progression on it since I think it is the most replayable and suitable mode for this genre. [*]Customizable camera control, can choose either WASD or middle mouse button (personally not a big thing to me, I am used to both, but for some, surprisingly, mouse control can be a big issue) [*]Enemies' design is decent. [/olist] [h3]Things I don't like and which can be improved:[/h3] [olist] [*]Camera control cannot be set to specific hotkey or mouse button (for example I want to be able move the camera with alt or mouse side buttons) [*]A huge thing and basically most annoying thing: no ghost buildings/markers for the buildings that are destroyed. If you had a huge swarm which destroyed most of your defense - you have to rebuild everything manually. The game is already microcontrol intensive and a lot of things are happening at once so sometimes you can forget, for example, to rebuild a forest cutting building which in turn can lower your resource income and you don't even notice this. We already have 'repair all' button and 'rebuild all' button would really be a huge upgrade and QoL. [*]The pacing feels very rushed. I played on normal and the first swarm comes in 10 minutes. This timing feels fine, but each subsequent swarm comes faster (in like 5 minutes intervals). Combining this with a fact that sometimes there spawns a worm on any place on the map which also has a timer to kill and you have to fight through other enemies' outposts to get to it, it puts a lot of stress on the player trying to achieve different things at once. Of course, there is an active pause, but it feels like you need to activate it constantly to be able to do everything. [*]The occassional small attacks at your base (not swarm but rather harassment units) could be manageable if not for the 2 previous things but because of them these attacks feel very annoying and frequent. I tried to manage it with units on patrol, but eventually the harassment force grew in size so I had to split my main force to reinforce the patrol units, which also feels very microintensive and not rewarding since your main force is constantly being drained. [*]The overall feeling for the economy is... I don't know, quite imbalanced? I saw some players point this out too but for personally for me it feels like you have to do A LOT to keep pace with swarm (also coming from the point 3). [/olist] I've quite enjoyed the demo before the release, but right now even with additional content and improvements I still cannot reccomend the game [b][i]yet[/i][/b] . Overall, with some improvements, QoL and balance changes I believe this game can really shine. It does have its own identity (a little bit bleak at the moment) and I think could become a staple title in the genre.
